correctness.rationale: Reconstructed stationary sign process from a two-sided equilibrium alternating renewal law, the unique stationary harmonic convolution Y_t=integral_{-infinity}^t e^{-(t-u)}sigma_u du, and entrance gap D=2-(Z+1)e^{-U}>=2(1-e^{-U}). The near-zero run law bounds Pr(D<delta)=O(delta^eta), establishing exponentially thin log-gap tails. The positive-age measure at a stationary observation is  ar F(a) da/(2m), leading to the exact H([log(D/eps)]_+) term. The negative sign contributes J([log(D/(2-eps))]_+) and is O(eps). Karamata/integration of regularly varying survival yields H(L)~c L^{1-beta}/(beta-1). Split D>=e^{-L/2} versus its exponentially rare complement, apply dominated convergence to the long-tail ratio, then reflection symmetry and tail integration yield both edge coefficients and divergent all positive reciprocal-gap moments. Checked that m=1/(beta-1),c=1 gives 1/2 for Lomax, and half-t density has m=1,c=1/2,beta=2 giving 1/4. The exact identity depends on the distribution of the stationary positive-run entrance gap and makes no finite-time claim.
